chains.summary: Each higher joy is a hundred times the one below. Each equals the joy of the learned person who is not struck by desire. Knowing that joy, one fears nothing. One is no longer tormented by wondering why one did not do right and why one did wrong.
chains.title: The measure of joy

verses.m: Now an inquiry into joy. Let there be a young man, good, well read, quick, firm and strong, and let this whole earth full of wealth be his: that is one measure of human joy. A hundred human joys make one joy of the human gandharvas, and so too is the joy of a learned one untouched by desire.
verses.sa: सैषाऽऽनन्दस्य मीमाꣳसा भवति । युवा स्यात्साधुयुवाऽध्यायकः । आशिष्ठो दृढिष्ठो बलिष्ठः । तस्येयं पृथिवी सर्वा वित्तस्य पूर्णा स्यात् । स एको मानुष आनन्दः । ते ये शतं मानुषा आनन्दाः । स एको मनुष्यगन्धर्वाणामानन्दः । श्रोत्रियस्य चाकामहतस्य ।

verses.m: That from which words turn back, along with the mind, not reaching it: whoever knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing at all.
verses.sa: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।

verses.m: Such a one is no longer tormented by the thought: why did I not do good? Why did I do wrong?
verses.sa: एतꣳह वाव न तपति । किमहꣳसाधु नाकरवम् । किमहं पापमकरवमिति ।

chains.summary: Alone, he was afraid. He reflected that since there is nothing other than him, he has nothing to fear. The fear left. Fear comes only from a second. Alone, he also found no joy, and one who is alone does not rejoice.
chains.title: Fear comes from a second

verses.m: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
verses.sa: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥

chains.summary: Pleasure brings fear of illness, family brings fear of decline, wealth brings fear of the king, honour brings fear of humiliation, strength brings fear of the enemy, beauty brings fear of age, learning brings fear of the debater, virtue brings fear of the slanderer, and the body brings fear of death. Everything on earth comes with fear, and dispassion alone is fearlessness.
chains.title: Everything comes with a fear

verses.m: In pleasure lies the fear of disease; in high birth, the fear of a fall; in wealth, fear of the king; in honour, fear of humiliation; in strength, fear of enemies; in beauty, fear of old age; in learning, fear of rival debaters; in virtue, fear of the wicked; in the body, fear of death. Everything in this world carries fear; only dispassion is fearless.
verses.sa: भोगे रोगभयं कुले च्युतिभयं वित्ते नृपालाद्भयं माने दैन्यभयं बले रिपुभयं रूपे जराया भयम् । शास्त्रे वादिभयं गुणे खलभयं काये कृतान्ताद्भयं सर्वं वस्तु भयान्वितं भुवि नृणां वैराग्यमेवाभयम् ॥

gloss: Fearlessness is first in the Gita's list of divine qualities (16.1). It is the Upanishad's mark of one who knows the joy of Brahman.

hero.m: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study, austerity and uprightness,
hero.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥

practices.m: Then he went into the court, remembering Ram's lotus feet, looking this way and that with a lion's gait, steady, brave, a mass of strength.
practices.sa: गयउ सभा दरबार तब सुमिरि राम पद कंज। सिंह ठवनि इत उत चितव धीर बीर बल पुंज ॥

practices.m: "The one who follows my teaching is truly my dear servant. But if I say anything unjust, brothers, put aside your fear and stop me."
practices.sa: सोइ सेवक प्रियतम मम सोई। मम अनुसासन मानै जोई॥ जौं अनीति कछु भाषौं भाई। तौ मोहि बरजहु भय बिसराई ॥

practices.m: I bow to you, Goddess, destroyer of great fear, who calms great hardship, whose very form is great compassion.
practices.sa: नमामि त्वामहं देवीं महाभयविनाशिनीम् । महादुर्गप्रशमनीं महाकारुण्यरूपिणीम् ॥
practices.why: Courage borrowed from the one bowed to.

practices.sa: Make your children strong from their very childhood;

practices.m: Here is the highest thing I can tell you, the purest and most valuable: never abandon what is right, not out of desire, not out of fear, not out of greed, not even to save your life.
practices.sa: इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि / पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् / न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभा- / द्धर्मं जह्याज्जीविस्यापि हेतोः

practices.m: Enter the city and do all your work, holding the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a one, poison turns to nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean shrinks to a hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
practices.sa: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
practices.why: Shows ocean becomes a hoofprint and fire turns cool.

practices.sa: Be brave and face everything — come good, come evil, both welcome,

practices.m: One from whom the world does not shrink and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.
practices.sa: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
practices.why: Names freedom from fear and agitation as a mark.

stories.l: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.
stories.s: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
stories.t: What becomes of one who falls from yoga

stories.l: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.
stories.s: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.

stories.l: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.
stories.s: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.

stories.l: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.
stories.s: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.
